rationale:
Evidence from iteration 8 (score 913.5, best so far): oval finishes 20/20 (progress 0.998, time 1.93 s, 1.0 line-loss events), s-bend finishes 20/20 (progress 0.996, time 2.29 s, 0.8 line-loss events), and slalom finishes 18/20 (progress 0.955, 2 off-track, control_effort 14.3). Moving the sensors to y=0.08 with kp 5.5 and kd 1.5 lifted slalom finishes from 9 to 18. Steering oscillation stayed at 0.24 to 0.32, well below the 0.5 warning level, so damping is not the limit. The remaining gap is slalom off-track ends, and the per-track score ceiling is roughly 940 to 950 at these times. Sensor y is now at the top of its allowed range, so the phase-lead lever is used up.

Change: narrow wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.11 m. Turn rate is (right wheel speed minus left wheel speed) divided by wheel_track, so for the same PWM differential the robot turns about 9 percent faster. This is an effective increase in steering authority without touching the gain values that are working. It is hypothesis (b)/(c) from iteration 7 and iteration 8, which both pointed at turn rate as the next limit once lag was reduced. Mass, sensor layout, controller gains, base_speed and line_loss are unchanged so the effect can be read against iteration 8. I considered lowering mass to 0.55 kg as well, but I held it back to keep the attribution clean.

Expected result: slalom progress rising to about 0.97 or more with off-track ends falling to 0 to 1 of 20, and oval and s-bend completion holding at 1.0. Because the robot turns harder, the wider-track baseline may show a small rise in line-loss events on the oval. Hypotheses: (a) if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.5, the extra turn rate is overcorrecting and kd should rise to about 1.7 or wheel_track should return to 0.12. (b) If slalom progress is flat versus iteration 8, turn rate is not the limit and the next lever is base_speed or line_loss handling. (c) If oval line_loss_events rise above 1.2, the robot is losing the tape at the edges and the sensor spread should widen slightly. Next measurements: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort per track, so I can see whether the faster turn rate reduces slalom drift and whether oval and s-bend time improves.
